title: Quantification of Retinal Nerve Fibre Layer Thickness on Optical Coherence Tomography with a Deep Learning Segmentation-Free Approach
summary: A ResNet34 model predicted retinal nerve fibre layer thickness directly from unsegmented OCT scans. In three held-out sets, predictions tracked conventional measurements on clean scans and more closely matched same-day good-quality references on scans with segmentation errors or other artefacts. This retrospective proof of concept did not test patient outcomes.
ai_technology: ResNet34 deep-learning model predicting retinal nerve fibre layer thickness from unsegmented optical coherence tomography scans

source_review.scope: Primary source full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version checked against primary publication metadata.

evidence.tested: The full study evaluated 25,285 B-scans from 1,338 eyes of 706 subjects in three test sets. Correlations with reference measurements were 0.983 on clean scans, 0.972 versus 0.829 for conventional segmentation on scans with segmentation errors, and 0.940 versus 0.640 on scans with other artefacts.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective test; references were conventional measurements or same-day good-quality scans. No downstream patient benefit was evaluated.
evidence.ai_role: A fine-tuned ResNet34 deep-learning model predicts global retinal nerve fibre layer thickness directly from unsegmented OCT B-scans.
